findings.title: A child as projected entitlement
findings.claim: The focus verb’s lineage claim makes “a child to the Rahman” the culmination of a nearby boast: in 19:77 offspring is paired with expected wealth, 19:78 tests the speaker’s warrant, and 19:80 answers the imagined gain with inheritance and a solitary return.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is an act of asserting child-lineage; the expectation of receiving wealth and offspring gives it an asset-like register, the covenant question tests entitlement, and inheritance and solitude remove what the speaker imagined retaining. Their contact makes the nearby moves explain one another.
findings.reader_payoff: The child claim becomes newly legible as imagined entitlement under a warrant, exposed as loss rather than durable possession.
findings.containment: 19:91 still reports that they attributed a child to the Rahman. The entitlement chain is an attributed contextual inference: 19:77–80 could also be consecutive accusations, and no legal ownership or actual covenant is established.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context coordinates and roots match the attributed trace; reader identity remains legacy_unbound. The trace coordinates and roots match 19:77, 19:78, 19:80, and the focus. Paired offspring and expected wealth, a tested warrant, and solitary return support a bounded entitlement reading; the attributed chain remains inferential.

findings.title: Sonship as protective affiliation
findings.claim: The focus attribution can also function as a bid for protective kinship: the pericope shows adopted gods sought for strength in 19:81, reversed into opponents in 19:82, while intercession is conditioned by covenant in 19:87.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is claimed child-lineage; the acquisition of protectors for strength, their reversal, and covenant-limited intercession give that alleged family tie the social work of patronage and access, then expose its guarantee as unstable.
findings.reader_payoff: The allegation carries a social aim as well as genealogical content: kinship is imagined as an access route.
findings.containment: The primary wording remains the report of an attributed child. The patronage link is an attributed inference; the allies and intercession sequence could indict separate practices rather than explain this clause.

findings.title: The universal servant sequence
findings.claim: The child attribution is placed against a sequence that leaves no genealogical exception: 19:92 denies the fit of taking a child, 19:93 calls every being a servant, 19:94 numbers them, and 19:95 brings each alone.
findings.mechanism: The focus child word proposes descent as exceptional nearness; the following universal quantifier, service relation, exhaustive reckoning, and solitary arrival contact that proposal as an exception the sequence does not allow.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus becomes the rejected exception in a sequence that moves from universal service to individual accounting.
findings.containment: The focus still states the child attribution; whether 19:93–95 are a relational answer or only judgment logistics remains open. The lexical slave echo is a secondary word-level resonance and does not identify the alleged child as a slave.

findings.title: Affection bestowed rather than inherited
findings.claim: The Rahman named in the focus is again the giver in 19:96, where trust and good work are met by love He causes; against the assigned child, the pericope offers nearness as bestowed affection among agents rather than blood.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers al-Rahman and waladan place mercy and inherited relation in the same clause; in 19:96 the Rahman makes affection for those who believe and do good. The new proximity is conditioned by trust and action and created as affection, changing alleged kinship into a bestowed social bond.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus names not just a family claim but a nearby mode of relation from 19:96: affection made by the Rahman.
findings.containment: The 19:96 line may begin a separate consolatory movement instead of answering the child claim; this is a nearby comparison, not an assertion that it directly rebuts 19:91.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context coordinates and roots match the attributed trace; reader identity remains legacy_unbound. The focus roots and every 19:96 trace coordinate match. The repeated Rahman title, believing and repairing agents, causative making, and affection form a specific nearby relation; the possibility of a new consolatory movement remains open.
